title: [R3-6 family] review.classify_replan_delta grants CARRY_FORWARD on caller-supplied evidence and a caller-supplied canonicalizer allow-list
description:
FILED BY architect-a69740e0 on 2026-08-28 while planning task-08efb6f0 (the CARRY evidence-reader row), measured at HEAD 7f062869. Board search: no open row names review-delta.ts or the caller-supplied-evidence path. Filed rather than absorbed because it is a different subsystem (review, not supersession) and a different authority boundary.

THE MECHANISM, measured symbol by symbol. `classifyReplanDelta` (apps/daemon/src/review/review-delta.ts:54-113) reads its nodes from the request payload at :56 (`payloadArray(request.payload, "nodes")`), `parseNodes` (:30-41) takes each node's `evidence` verbatim from `value["evidence"]` at :34 with no validation beyond `isPlainJsonObject`, and :88 hands that object straight to `evaluateCarryForward(node.evidence, supported)`. The second argument is ALSO caller-supplied: `supportedCanonicalizerVersions` is read from the same payload at :57.

WHY THAT IS A GRANT AND NOT A CHECK. `evaluateCarryForward` (packages/core/src/policy/approval-invalidation.ts:173-196) is a pure VALIDATOR of a supplied fact set — its own module header states the division of labour verbatim: "Core VALIDATES AND APPLIES a supplied impact set; it never computes one. Design 265 makes the graph diff the daemon's job." It returns `valid: true` exactly when `sourceHash === targetHash`, the four booleans (`dependenciesPresent`, `environmentClosureUnchanged`, `policySliceUnchanged`, `predecessorResultUnchanged`) are all true, and `versions.includes(input.canonicalizerVersion)`. Every one of those is under caller control here, INCLUDING the version allow-list that is supposed to fence the last condition. So a caller submits seven self-asserted facts plus a list containing its own canonicalizer version and obtains a CARRY_FORWARD classification — the classification that carries a predecessor's proof forward instead of re-qualifying the node.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME BOUNDARY THE FAMILY ALREADY DEFENDS. `apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-supersede-dispositions.ts:12-19` refuses to emit CARRY for exactly this reason, in its own words: "CARRY is the one kind that GRANTS something ... the kernel will only accept it with `safeCarry` evidence that `evaluateCarryForward` validates — seven facts ... This tree has no durable reader for any of them, and DoD 1 forbids the request supplying carry authority, so emitting CARRY would mean inventing the evidence." The supersession path fails closed on that rule. The review path does not apply it at all.

MEASURED SCOPE OF THE GAP, so the fix is not planned against a fantasy. Of the seven facts, `dependenciesPresent`, `environmentClosureUnchanged` and `predecessorResultUnchanged` have ZERO daemon non-test hits (no producer, no reader, no durable record; only type members at packages/core/src/policy/approval-contract.ts:104-107), and `policySliceUnchanged` exists only in the activation subsystem and not per node. So this row CANNOT be fixed by "read them from the store instead" — those readers do not exist and task-08efb6f0 measures that gap. The reachable fix is to FAIL CLOSED: refuse the caller-supplied evidence channel with a stable code rather than validate it, and derive `supportedCanonicalizerVersions` from the server (`CANONICAL_JSON_VERSION`, packages/contracts/src/phase0-evidence-contract.ts:86) rather than from the payload. Whether the handler should then refuse every delta, or only refuse the CARRY_FORWARD outcome while still classifying INVALIDATED, is a scoping question for whoever plans this — measure the downstream consumers of `DeltaNodeClassification` before choosing.

RELATED, do not duplicate: task-08efb6f0 owns the supersession-side carry evidence assembler and the measurement of which facts are durably readable. This row owns the review handler's caller-supplied channel. If the two converge on a shared assembler, compose it — do not build a second one.

OWNERSHIP AT FILING: `apps/daemon/src/review/review-delta.ts` (113 lines) has ZERO live file-field claims and is porcelain-clean. Re-measure at claim; stale by default.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK on disk at claim, recorded in a row comment: review-delta.ts:88 still passes `node.evidence` (read from the request payload at :34/:56) into `evaluateCarryForward`, and :57 still reads `supportedCanonicalizerVersions` from the payload — else adopt the fixing commit and report blocked as duplicate. Also re-measure the four absent facts (`dependenciesPresent`, `environmentClosureUnchanged`, `predecessorResultUnchanged` return zero daemon non-test hits; `policySliceUnchanged` only in the activation path) and record the counts, because the fix shape depends on them still being absent.

A production-surface reproduction lands RED FIRST: an arm driving the real review handler with a fully self-asserted evidence object (all four booleans true, sourceHash === targetHash, a caller-named canonicalizerVersion) plus a caller-supplied `supportedCanonicalizerVersions` containing that same version, asserting it currently receives a CARRY_FORWARD classification. That arm is the reviewer's claim executed on the production edge and it must be committed, not a deleted probe.

The handler FAILS CLOSED on the caller-supplied channel: the evidence object is no longer accepted from the payload as carry authority, and `supportedCanonicalizerVersions` is derived from the server (CANONICAL_JSON_VERSION) rather than read from the request. The refusal asserts an exact stable reason code AND the refusing layer, since more than one layer can refuse a bad delta. Do NOT fabricate the four facts that have no durable source in either direction — a `true` invents authority and a `false` fabricates a measured negative that the core turns into a specific reason code.

The downstream blast radius is measured and named BEFORE the fix, not discovered mid-step: grep every consumer of `DeltaNodeClassification` and every caller of the review delta handler, name them in the plan's owned-path roster, and state whether INVALIDATED classification still proceeds or the whole handler refuses. If naming every consumer would breach the row's path cap, that is a split signal at plan time.

DIVERGENCE (epic rail 7A): the new refusal has an arm where it is the ONLY mechanism that can refuse — the payload is otherwise well-shaped, the nodes are unique, the ledger is readable, a round exists and expectedVersion matches, so REVIEW_PAYLOAD_INVALID, REVIEW_DELTA_NODES_EMPTY, REVIEW_DELTA_NODE_DUPLICATED, REVIEW_LINEAGE_UNREADABLE, REVIEW_REPLAN_WITHOUT_ROUND and REVIEW_EXPECTED_VERSION_STALE all pass. State why none of them answers first. Mutation drill: delete the new refusal and the red-first arm must go RED again with its exact code; a green drill is a FINDING, not a pass.

Gates standalone and unpiped with nonzero counts: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0 quoting its `$ tsc` echo, and `(cd apps/daemon && pnpm exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/review/...)` with `Test Files`/`Tests` count lines quoted — the root vitest include has no apps/**, so a bare `pnpm test` runs zero daemon tests. Repo-wide red path-attributed merge-base versus HEAD with an empty owned-path intersection; every production file stays under 400 lines; explicit-pathspec commit.
taskRails: Never fabricate the four carry-forward facts that have no durable source (`dependenciesPresent`, `environmentClosureUnchanged`, `predecessorResultUnchanged`, and `policySliceUnchanged` per node). A `true` invents carry authority; a `false` fabricates a measured negative that `evaluateCarryForward` translates into a specific reason code. Absence and negation are different answers and must stay different — refuse instead.

The request may never supply carry authority. That is the family's standing rule and the reason `graph-supersede-dispositions.ts:12-19` refuses to emit CARRY at all. Evidence comes from the store or the server, never from the caller — and that includes the `supportedCanonicalizerVersions` allow-list, which fences the last of the seven conditions.
Do not build a second carry-evidence assembler. task-08efb6f0 owns the supersession-side one; if this row needs the same derivation, compose it and say so in #architects rather than duplicating it.

Do not relax or reinterpret `evaluateCarryForward` in packages/core. It is a pure validator by design and its module header states the division of labour verbatim; the defect is the daemon handing it caller bytes, not the core validating what it is given.

implementationPlan.description:
THE RED-FIRST PRODUCTION-SURFACE REPRODUCTION (DoD 2, epic rail 3). This arm IS the reviewer's claim executed on the production edge, and it MUST BE COMMITTED — a deleted probe is a lead, never evidence.

In apps/daemon/src/review/review-delta.test.ts (289 lines), drive `runReviewCommand` (the production entry, review-services.ts) with kind `qualification.replan` — NOT the `review.classify_replan_delta` in this row's title, which is not a real kind (review-services.ts:188 registers the handler under `qualification.replan`). Everything else well-formed so the delta commits.

ASSERT THE GRANT, not merely a success: the returned classification for that node is exactly `"CARRY_FORWARD"`, and `reasonCodes` is EMPTY (that is what `valid: true` means at approval-invalidation.ts:196 — `valid: reasonCodes.length === 0`). Asserting only "the command succeeded" would stay green after the fix and prove nothing.

Use a canonicalizerVersion that is NOT `CANONICAL_JSON_VERSION` ("moe-canonical-json/1"). That is the whole point of the reproduction: the caller's own allow-list is what admits the caller's own version, so a fixture that happens to name the real version would pass for the wrong reason and would keep passing after step 4 derives the list from the server.

After step 4 this arm inverts to assert the refusal. Keep it as ONE arm that changes its expectation, not two arms — and quote its RED output in the step note before touching production.

implementationPlan.description:
THE FIX — apps/daemon/src/review/review-delta.ts (113 lines; stays far under 400). Implements the ruling in comment-bbc3667f, whose five numbered points are the specification.

(1) REFUSE THE CHANNEL, DO NOT IGNORE IT. A payload whose `nodes[]` carry an `evidence` key, or which carries `supportedCanonicalizerVersions` at all, refuses with step 3's code at `DAEMON_INGRESS`. Silently dropping the keys is forbidden: a silently ignored spoof is indistinguishable from an honoured one at the call site.
(2) `parseNodes` (:30-41) narrows `DeltaNodeInput` to `{ nodeRef }`. Delete the `evidence: JsonObject` member and the `isPlainJsonObject(evidence)` admission; keep the nodeRef checks and the duplicate-nodeRef guard at :71 exactly as they are.
(3) DELETE the `evaluateCarryForward` call at :88 and the `@moe/core` import at :2. This is NOT epic rail 7A's forbidden "deleting the redundant call": that rule protects a guard whose removal a mutant would exploit. Here the call is the DEFECT ITSELF — it is a validator being handed caller bytes, and the row exists to stop that. taskRail 4 forbids EDITING `evaluateCarryForward`; it does not require calling it. Say so in the module doc so a later reader does not restore it.
(4) Every node classifies `"INVALIDATED"`. `reasonCodes` is server-minted from the family's own vocabulary — `CARRY_EVIDENCE_FACT_UNREADABLE` plus the missing-fact names, both reachable through `carry-forward-evidence.ts`'s exports (`CarryForwardEvidenceCode`, `missingCarryForwardFacts`, `CarryForwardDurableFact`). COMPOSE those exports; do NOT re-spell the strings locally and do NOT build a second assembler (taskRail 3). Do not call `assembleCarryForwardEvidence` itself: it needs graph-revision `Authorities` the handler's context (review-ledger.ts:64-69 = `{ledger, request, store}`) does not have, and its answer is unconditionally a refusal anyway.
(5) `sourceHash`/`targetHash` become `""`, and `stringOf` (:43-45) is deleted with its last caller. Document WHY in the module doc: no server hash source exists at this seam, the caller's copy is what is being removed, the field stays a string so the durable record and `parseClassification` (review-read-model.ts:122-132) are unchanged, and an empty hash grants nothing because no comparison is performed any more.

REWRITE THE MODULE DOC AT :9-23. It currently says "THE CLASSIFICATION IS NOT DECIDED HERE" and cites the core's division of labour — after this change that paragraph is false and would read as an invitation to restore the call. State instead that carry authority is unobtainable server-side today (carry-forward-evidence.ts:65-74), that CARRY_FORWARD is therefore unreachable through this handler exactly as `graph-supersede-dispositions.ts:12-19` refuses to emit CARRY, and that the caller may never supply it.

Do NOT remove `"CARRY_FORWARD"` from `DELTA_CLASSIFICATIONS` (review-contracts.ts:120). The union stays total; the value is simply unproducible without authority, and deleting it would make a future authorised carry a breaking change.

THE DIVERGENCE ARM (DoD 5, epic rail 7A) — its own step, because a fixture that merely reaches the new refusal proves the system refuses, not that THIS guard refuses.

Build one arm in review-delta.test.ts where the new refusal is the ONLY mechanism that can answer. Every other fence in the handler must be PASSED, and the arm's comment must state that and why:

  REVIEW_LINEAGE_UNREADABLE (:75) — ledger readable (drive real rounds through the fixtures, do not hand-write bytes).
  REVIEW_REPLAN_WITHOUT_ROUND (:80) — at least one recorded round.

The ONLY thing wrong with the request is that a node carries `evidence` (and, in a second case, that the payload carries `supportedCanonicalizerVersions`). Assert the EXACT new code AND the `DAEMON_INGRESS` layer — more than one layer can refuse a bad delta, so the layer is half the assertion.

ORDERING HAZARD, and it decides whether this arm is real: step 4's new check must sit where `REVIEW_PAYLOAD_INVALID` cannot answer first. `parseNodes` currently returns `undefined` for any node it dislikes and :69 converts that into REVIEW_PAYLOAD_INVALID — so if the evidence check is folded into `parseNodes`'s undefined return, the new code is UNREACHABLE and this arm will fail with the wrong code. The evidence rejection must be a distinct branch with its own return. Note that explicitly in the arm's comment; it is the single most likely way this fix lands broken-but-green.

The drill for this arm is step 8 D1.
